audits.title: Differences in rates of uptake of NICE clinical guidelines between Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) and Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) as evidenced by National Diabetes Audit of England and Wales
audits.standard: NICE targets: HbA1c =<7.5% (58.5 mmol/mol), blood pressure <140/80mmHg, cholesterol <5mmol/l; at least annual monitoring of HbA1c, blood pressure, cholesterol, albumin:creatinine ratio, smoking status and BMI
audits.setting: Diabetes specialist services and GP surgeries submitting National Diabetes Audit data

cycle1.result: T2DM patients had higher odds of meeting clinical targets than T1DM in all five years except cholesterol <5mmol/l; largest difference for HbA1c =<7.5% in 2015-16 (OR 3.43, 95% CI 3.39 to 3.47)

audits.other_findings: Analysis of five annual NDA collections (1,739,175 patients in 2013-14 rising to 3,357,055 in 2017-18) comparing T1DM and T2DM.
audits.citation: Hayward RC, Watkins J, Ariti C. Differences in rates of uptake of NICE clinical guidelines between Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) and Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) as evidenced by National Diabetes Audit of England and Wales. . 2020. doi:10.1101/2020.08.05.20168914.

audits.title: Cooperation between general practitioners and diabetologists and clinical audit improve the management of type 2 diabetic patients.
audits.standard: Consensus guidelines based on French St Vincent recommendations
audits.setting: 73 volunteer general practitioners in Essonne

cycle1.result: Standards not met for several criteria; lack of HbA1c standardisation and delayed intervention for inadequate glucose control.

audits.intervention: Cooperative protocols for foot care, nephropathy and retinopathy prevention, HbA1c standardisation and a primary care educational programme.

cycle2.result: Improvement in foot care (+33.6%), quality (+39.9%), HbA1c prescription (+11.9%), blood pressure control (+11.9%), lipids (+12.8%); early interventions for poor glucose control +10.5%.

audits.other_findings: Gaps persisted in screening for complications, diet counselling and patient education.
audits.citation: Varroud-Vial M, Mechaly P, Joannidis S, Chapiro O, Pichard S, Lebigot A, et al.. Cooperation between general practitioners and diabetologists and clinical audit improve the management of type 2 diabetic patients. Diabetes Metab. 1999;25(1):55-63. PMID: 10335424.

cycle1.result: Diagnosis made in 63% with two raised fasting glucose values; 87% had annual check-up; 36% satisfactory metabolic control.

audits.citation: Hänninen J, Keinänen-Kiukaanniemi S, Takala J. Population-based audit of non-insulin-dependent diabetic patients aged under 65 years in primary health care. Scand J Prim Health Care. 1998;16(4):227-232. doi:10.1080/028134398750003007. PMID: 9932316.
